summary: The unsigned→signed data conversion for `_Unsigned=False` is correct and the values now decode properly, but the `warnings.warn` call ends up inside the new `elif` branch (16-space indent, no `else`), so it fires the misleading 'not of integer type, ignoring attribute' warning right after a successful conversion and is no longer emitted for genuinely non-integer `_Unsigned` variables.

issues.description: The unchanged `warnings.warn(...)` context line sits at the same indent as the new `signed_dtype` body, so it is now part of the `elif data.dtype.kind == 'u' and unsigned == 'false':` block. After correctly converting u→i it STILL emits 'variable %r has _Unsigned attribute but is not of integer type. Ignoring attribute.' — directly contradicting the action taken. Since the warning was the exact symptom reported in the issue, the user's pydap case keeps seeing the SerializationWarning even though values are now right. The warning should live in a separate `else:` branch (i.e. `if kind=='i': ...

By absorbing the former `else: warn` into the `elif`, the original warning for legitimately unsupported `_Unsigned` cases (e.g. float dtype carrying an `_Unsigned` attribute, the case shown in the issue's `engine='pydap'` float32 example) is dropped — those now decode silently with no diagnostic, a behavioral regression versus the prior code.
No inline comment documents the `_Unsigned=False` OPeNDAP/netCDF-c 'hack' being handled here; a one-line comment referencing the convention would aid future maintainers.
